verdicts.reason: Quotes are accurate but the reconciliation is explicit and repeated across the tree, and it settles the exact forcedInvention. 18.03.01-advance-checklist.md:194 D-07 defines the term: "'block' means 'requires an override that goes on the record'". 18.03.05-advance-freeze-change-control.md Edge Cases: "Hard item still open but Producer wants to freeze | Freeze allowed with an explicit override + mandatory reason", and its DT-04 REJECTS "Freeze is a hard gate requiring zero open items". Decisively, the state owner answers the auto-freeze question outright: 18.01-event-record-lifecycle.md:49 "| `advanced` | 18 (Producer) | Producer **freezes** the advance (18.03.05 D-01) | Production pack frozen. Edits become change-control events, never blocked (18.03.05 D-02). |", :50 "Auto-freeze fires if never frozen", :80 "auto-freezes with open items recorded as unresolved (18.03.05)", and D-05 at :177 "The freeze is the `advancing → advanced` transition, and it is **unilateral by the Producer**". Every domain-CX sentence the finding cites as 'unqualified' in fact carries the override clause in the same sentence (show-production-touring-cx.md:306 "...overrides record what wasn't resolved and who accepted the risk"), and 18.16:72 says "can block", not 'blocks'. 18.16's edge case is therefore consistent with, not contradictory to, D-07. Two implementers reading the tree converge on an overridable, record-generating gate.

Quotes verified verbatim at 18.18-post-show-report.md:50 and :58. But only a numeric constant is unstated — the behaviour either window governs is fully specified: :58 "unanswered discrepancies proceed on the corroboration path without the Operator's input, never blocked by their silence", and :50 the report is non-blocking ("Event still settles"). The fairness decision (silence never blocks) is made; the duration is a tunable. The file itself establishes that exact window values are a later-layer concern — :102 D-05 "Exact window `[PENDING — /write-be-spec]`" and :57 "an editable window (e.g. 7 days)" — so the same class of value is explicitly routed to /write-be-spec. Two implementers build the identical system modulo a config constant; nothing about product behaviour must be invented.

Both alleged inversions are explicitly resolved one level down, in the sub-domain index a spec writer for those leaves must read. 18.04: 18.04-riders-index.md:40 "| 18.04.03 Access Rider | ✅ Full (own only) | 👁️ Read-only (scoped) | 👁️ Read-only (need-to-know) | ❌ None |" plus the deliberate note at :51-53 ("the only child where the **Musician outranks the Producer** … a TM cannot author, edit, or trade away someone else's access need … deliberate") and D-03 at :61. 18.06: 18.06-setlist-show-files-index.md:41 "| 18.06.03 Show File Custody | ⚙️ Config | ✅ Full | 👁️ Read-only (durations only) | ❌ None |" and :42 "| 18.06.04 Performed Setlist Capture | … | 👁️ Read-only | 👁️ Read-only (published only) |", with the reconciling note at :52-54 ("the **setlist is the act's private property** — the Operator has no access to 18.06.01, only to the *durations* it produces via the schedule"). The domain matrix rows are sub-domain-granularity roll-ups and the domain index states this at show-production-touring-index.md:106 ("Access icons are shorthand; detailed per-role behavior lives in each feature file's **Role Lens**"). The 18.03/Musician case IS tracked precisely because it has no such reconciling note; these two do, so the tracking is consistent rather than arbitrary.

The dangling pointer is real (18.05-stage-plot-input-list-cx.md:73 ends "Not yet settled — see Open Questions." and the file's headings run CX-01…CX-04 → Rejected Pairs (:98) → Notes → Related Specs, with no Open Questions section), but no behaviour is left undetermined. The same line supplies the answer — "the mix is authoritative (a wedge exists because a mix needs it), the plot positions it" — and the cross-cut map row states it as settled fact at :12 "wedges are plot items that exist because a mix needs them", consistent with 18.05 index D-04 ("A mix is defined as channels (from the input list) sent to a position (on the plot)"). The named consequence is asserted affirmatively, not conditionally, at :74 "Mix added on a wedge → plot item appears → footprint changes → stage-dimension diff may newly fail. A monitor decision can therefore make the act not fit the stage, which is a non-obvious chain worth specifying." Two implementers converge on the same model and the same diff behaviour; the 'unresolved' label flags a modelling preference, not an open product decision.

The quotes are accurate, but the exclusion is stated in the owning unit's own CX — a first-class spec document in this tree — and in four further places, and the feature files use the excluded term rather than count(roster). 18.08-crew-credentials-cx.md:55 states the requirement and :86 restates it in Notes for agents. 18.08's own sub-domain index treats it as settled vocabulary: 18.08-crew-credentials-index.md:72 "the **local-labour exclusion** means they draw no per diem". The consumer the finding names does not derive from count(roster): 18.04.02-hospitality-rider.md:51 "| Rider written for the band, but crew eat too | … | 'Rider covers 5 — the **touring party** is 9' |" and :27 "a five-piece doesn't silently under-cater a nine-person **touring party**". The producing feature publishes the same typed quantity: 18.08.01-crew-roster-call-times.md:20 "Sees the **touring party size** and roles for their date". Corroborated again at 18.12.01 D-02, 18.12.02, 18.12-travel-logistics-index.md:58 and 18.13-tour-finance-cx.md:75. An implementer has the answer in the unit's cx.md, the unit's index, and the consumer's own edge case.

Quotes verified (18.09-backline-gear-manifest-cx.md:74 "Genuinely unresolved.", :104 "has no good answer yet"), and the coverage claim is correct — 18.09 index Q-01/Q-02/Q-03, 18.09.01 Q-01 and 18.09.03 Q-01/Q-02 are all struck through. But the trigger is stated one line above, in the same CX block: :73 "**Trigger chain**: Loss confirmed → manifest updated for remaining dates → diffs re-run → new shortfalls → sourcing." The confirmation semantics are supplied by the owning leaf: 18.09.03-load-out-loss-damage.md:45 "Losses are provisional until confirmed; closing the log is normal", with :44 and the Partial state (:60 "54 of 60 confirmed — 6 unaccounted") showing an unconfirmed item sits in the check, not in the manifest. Every reasonable reading is therefore mutate-on-confirmation; the CX's 'unresolved' marks a product tension (phantom shortfall vs late hire), not an undetermined behaviour an implementer must invent.

Verified and nothing in the tree resolves it. 18.13-tour-finance-cx.md:37 verbatim: "A receipt captured offline and synced days later lands in a float that has since been reconciled. Does it reopen the reconciliation? Unresolved — and real, because offline capture guarantees late arrivals." The precondition is a ratified decision, not speculation — 18.13.03-expense-receipt-capture.md:45 "| Offline at a petrol station | Must queue and sync" — so the case is guaranteed. Both leaves describe reconciliation as terminal without covering a late arrival: 18.13.01-per-diems-float.md:37 "At tour end the float reconciles: opening + income − payouts − receipts = what's in the envelope" and 18.13.03:36 "At the end of the week the float reconciles". The nearest edge case is a different one — 18.13.01:43 "| Float doesn't reconcile | The normal outcome; needs a variance with a reason, not silent absorption |" — which constrains how variance is recorded but does not say whether a closed period reopens. No open question covers it: 18.13-tour-finance-index.md Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 are ownership boundary, band P&L visibility and holding the float; 18.13.01 Q-01 is holding/advancing the float (Q-02 struck); 18.13.03 Q-01/Q-02 are build/buy OCR and scope. The tracking is bare prose with no owner and no deferral target, so it fails the tracked-deferral test, and reopen vs post-to-current vs prior-period-adjustment yield three different cash positions from identical inputs. Warning rather than blocking: it is one edge, and no two normative statements are in conflict — the spec is simply silent.
